indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2. 2.1.2: Recognize the relationship between the Earth and the Sun
indicator.objective: Identify sources of light to the earth

skills.description: Identify sources of light to the Earth
Sort sources of light into natural and artificial
Recognise the sun as the main and most important source of light to the Earth
Explain simply why we need light

misconceptions: The moon makes its own light.
Lightning and fireflies are not sources of light.
Only the sun is a source of light.
We only need light at night.
A mirror is a source of light.

questions.stem: What is the main source of light to the Earth?
hints: It shines during the day.
It is very bright and hot.
questions.explanation: The sun is the main and most important source of light to the Earth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the moon is the main source of light.

questions.stem: Which of these can give us light at night?
hints: It uses a battery.
You use it during a power outage.
questions.explanation: A torch is a source of light that we can use at night.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a mirror makes its own light.

questions.stem: Why do we need light?
hints: When it is dark, can you see well?
Light helps our eyes.
questions.explanation: We need light so that we can see things around us.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think we only need light for plants.

questions.stem: Name a source of light you use in your home.
hints: You switch it on.
It is on the ceiling.
questions.explanation: An electric bulb is a source of light used in homes.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think objects like chairs give light.

questions.stem: Is the sun a natural or artificial source of light?
hints: Was it made by people?
It is in the sky.
questions.explanation: The sun is a natural source of light because it is not made by humans.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know the difference between natural and artificial.

questions.stem: Which of these is an artificial source of light?
hints: It is made by people.
You light it with a match.
questions.explanation: A candle is an artificial source of light because it is made by humans.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think lightning is artificial.

questions.stem: Which of these is a natural source of light?
hints: It happens in the sky.
It is very bright and comes with thunder.
questions.explanation: Lightning is a natural source of light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider lightning a source of light.

questions.stem: Which of these insects produces its own light?
hints: You see them glowing at night.
They have a light on their tail.
questions.explanation: Fireflies are natural sources of light because they can produce their own light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know that some insects can produce light.

questions.stem: Why is the sun called the main source of light?
options: Because it is the biggest and brightest source for the Earth
Because it is in the sky
Because we cannot look at it directly
hints: Is there any other light as bright as the sun?
It lights up the whole Earth during the day.
questions.explanation: The sun is the main source because it provides the most light to the Earth.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a torch is a main source because they use it often.

questions.stem: How does light from the sun help plants?
options: It helps them grow and make food
hints: Plants turn towards the sun.
They need light to make their food.
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight to make their own food and to grow healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants only need water and soil.

questions.stem: Sort these sources of light into natural and artificial: Sun, Torch, Stars, Bulb.
answer: natural: sun, stars; artificial: torch, bulb
hints: Which ones are made by humans?
Which ones are found in nature?
questions.explanation: The sun and stars are natural. A torch and a bulb are artificial (made by humans).
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all bright things are natural.

questions.stem: What is the main source of light for the Earth?
hints: It comes out during the day.
It is a star.
questions.explanation: The sun is the main source of light for the Earth.

questions.stem: Ama says 'The moon makes its own light.' Why is she wrong?
options: Because the moon reflects light from the sun
Because the moon is too small
Because the moon only comes out at night
Because the moon is not in the sky
hints: Does the moon have fire on it?
It shines because the sun shines on it.
questions.explanation: The moon does not make its own light. It shines by reflecting light from the sun.
questions.misconception: Pupils often think the moon is a source of its own light.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a source of light?
hints: Does a mirror make its own light?
It only bounces light back.
questions.explanation: A mirror is not a source of light. It only reflects light that comes from other sources.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a mirror produces light because it looks bright.

questions.stem: What would happen to the Earth if there was no source of light at all?
options: It would be completely dark and we could not see
It would be covered in ice
hints: Think about a room with no windows at night.
No light means no vision.
questions.explanation: Without any source of light, the Earth would be completely dark, and it would be impossible to see anything.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think we can see in the dark naturally.

questions.stem: Why is a candle an artificial source of light?
options: Because it is made by humans
Because it is made of wax
hints: Can you find a candle growing in a forest?
Was it made in a factory?
questions.explanation: A candle is artificial because it is manufactured by humans, not found in nature.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think anything that burns is natural.

questions.stem: Name two natural sources of light.
hints: Look up at the sky during the day.
Look up at the sky at night.
questions.explanation: The sun, stars, lightning, and fireflies are natural sources of light.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name torches or bulbs, which are artificial.

questions.stem: Explain why the sun is a more important source of light than a torch.

criteria.description: States that the sun gives light to the whole Earth
States that a torch only gives light to a small area for a short time

hints: How much of the Earth does the sun light up?
How far can a torch shine?
questions.explanation: The sun is more important because it lights up the entire Earth during the day, while a torch only provides a small amount of light for a short time.

questions.stem: Why is a mirror NOT a source of light?

criteria.description: States that a mirror only reflects light
States that it cannot produce its own light

hints: What happens if you put a mirror in a completely dark room?
It bounces light.
questions.explanation: A mirror is not a source of light because it cannot produce its own light. It only reflects light from other sources.

questions.stem: A firefly produces its own light. Is it a natural or artificial source of light?
options: Natural, because it is a living thing found in nature
Artificial, because it has a small battery
Natural, because it is made by humans
Artificial, because it glows at night
hints: Is a firefly a living creature?
Does it come from a factory?
questions.explanation: A firefly is a natural source of light because it is a living organism that produces light naturally.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think glowing means artificial.
